paper.summary: The ACCV 2026 draft (/home/spencer/Projects/OnlineSyntheticCorrespondence/ACCV_2026/main.tex, 1059 lines, compiles to 23 pp + 9 pp supplement) argues a single thesis: which synthetic training set transfers best to a real correspondence benchmark is regime-conditional, because the training regime determines which of two directed motion-mismatch costs the model pays. In BFV motion space (4-D normalized flow vectors), d_T->B measures off-target mass (precision-analogous) and d_B->T measures missing support (recall-analogous). The "regime-direction principle": from-scratch models pay BOTH costs (so candidate utility tracks the sum d_TB+d_BT, which equals the symmetric average), while a pretrained image-feature backbone forgives off-target mass, leaving missing support as the sole cost; because the two distances are anti-correlated across natural sources (mean Spearman ~-0.35, tight-vs-broad tradeoff), averaging the forgiven cost back in actively corrupts pretrained rankings. Argument structure: Sec 1 states the principle and 5 contributions; Sec 2 positions vs Mayer et al. (undirected), transferability estimation (symmetric/classification-only), and precision-recall divergences (diagnostic, not predictive); Sec 3 defines the 99-model / 891-measurement transfer study (CATs++, RAFT, GLU-Net in 9 variants x 11 sources x 9 benchmarks, peak PCK@0.05, Middlebury excluded), the two NN distances, support-vs-density estimator argument, and the anchor+ranking decomposition; Sec 4 establishes the flip (8 of 9 variants, exact permutation p=0.0286, group means scratch rho[dTB]=+0.42 vs pretrained rho[dBT]=+0.61 / rho[dTB]=-0.08), estimator replication, DINO appearance null (p=0.43), and the two-cost mechanism; Sec 5 derives the fit-free regime-aware selection policy (rank by dTB+dBT scratch, dBT pretrained), shows it best on all three hold-out protocols (rho 0.52/0.52/0.50), frames rho~0.5 as the reproducibility ceiling (pretrained fraction 1.08 = parity with retraining a sibling; 73-76% of a 3-architecture consensus at ceiling 0.732), recovers the sign structure with per-regime 2-coefficient OLS, and translates to decisions (median top-1 regret 1.2-2.8 PCK vs 13.9 random); Sec 6 splits absolute prediction into anchors (units) + policy (order), MAE 9.3 / r 0.88 LOTO, pretrained MAE 8.2 / r 0.90; Sec 7 gives interventional support: a pre-registered out-of-sample test on a never-seen generated grid where the off-target cost ranks from-scratch sources on the one benchmark where it varies (FlyingThings rho +0.67, 3.1x spread, vs symmetric -0.28), a closed-loop render-free generator search (+0.93 predicted / +0.87 realized on KITTI-2015, null control -1.6), BFV construct validity (recovered camera-vs-object regimes match target physics), the trial19 case study (scratch rank 1/9 -> pretrained rank 3/9), and a motion x texture 2x2 showing specificity-not-magnitude; Sec 8 Limitations is unusually candid (8/9 flip, pretrained half observational-only and the grid's pretrained arm nominally favors the wrong direction, no interventional test of the scratch missing-support cost, 2 backbone architectures, 3 pre-registered FlowFormer predictions); Sec 9 concludes "select with the policy, design with the direction." All 8 main-text \input tables and all 11 main + 4 supp figures exist on disk. The biggest audit findings: (1) tab_decomp's two object-motion/matte cells (83.2, 42.1) were harvested at 00:02 Jun 11 from a from-scratch run launched 21:08 Jun 10 that was still training (val CSV last written 23:57, exact in-flight maxima 83.2400 / 42.0822) — provisional numbers in a main-text table; (2) Sec 7 prose quotes the grid's pretrained-arm point estimates as +0.64/+0.31/+0.43 but the current intervention_oos.csv TT means are +0.64/+0.21/+0.37 (the CSV is explicitly flagged as live in DRAFT_NOTES); (3) the supplement is one reframe behind the main text — it still says the pretrained grid arm has "only three sources", quotes pre-policy rule rhos (0.50/0.51/0.51), says "1,458 models" where main says 99, uses the banned "fine-tuned" wording, and still makes the "rank training sets better than retraining" claim the main text deliberately retracted to "parity"; (4) two supp references from main (KuBasic/pretrained 2x2 replication; 95% bootstrap CIs for Table 3) point to content that does not exist in supp_main.tex; (5) smaller presentation bugs: RAFT shown with a backbone checkmark inside the from-scratch block of Tables 1-2, the policy bolded as best in tab_utility's both-held pairwise column where matched-direction is higher (0.79 vs 0.78), and a tab_law caption claim ("4 of 9 rows... all from-scratch or near-neutral") whose fourth row is actually pretrained CATs++ frozen.

claims.claim: The directional flip holds in 8 of 9 training variants; exact permutation p=0.029 (abstract) / p=0.0286 excluding RAFT from the labeling, p=0.0079 with RAFT in the scratch group (Sec 4); it vanishes in DINO appearance space (flip statistic +0.018, p=0.43).

claims.claim: Scratch regime: symmetric average is the best group-mean predictor (+0.50 vs +0.42 for dTB alone); pretrained: symmetric mean dragged from +0.61 down to +0.39; strongest cells pretrained GLU-Net +0.26/+0.33 (sym) vs +0.67/+0.76 (dBT).
Estimator replication of the flip: epsilon-radius coverage at 4px/16px gives +0.65/+0.91, directional kNN-KL +0.30, all at the permutation floor p=0.0286.

Fit-free regime-aware policy (Eq. 3: D=dTB+dBT scratch, D=dBT pretrained) ranks held-out source / benchmark / both at rho 0.52/0.52/0.50, best of 9 predictor families; summed-distance-everywhere 0.44/0.44/0.46; FID/SW2/MMD 0.34/0.44/0.37; 13-feature motion ridge 0.22/0.36/0.23; appearance ridge -0.11/+0.19/-0.07.

Reproducibility-ceiling framing: same-regime retraining agreement (empirical oracle) is rho ~0.56-0.69; policy fraction 1.08 pretrained (0.612 vs oracle 0.564, claimed as parity) and 0.72 scratch (0.499 vs 0.698, headroom in scratch GLU-Net); vs cross-architecture consensus oracle (ceiling 0.732) policy recovers 73-76%. Verified against ceiling_oracles.csv (pretrained rule_rho mean 0.6124, O2 mean 0.5645) and CONSENSUS_POLICY.csv (fractions 0.762803/0.747084/0.727278, cross_arch_consensus_rho 0.732319).

Per-regime 2-coefficient OLS recovers the sign structure: scratch w[dTB]=-7.57, w[dBT]=-1.08; pretrained w[dTB]=-0.82, w[dBT]=-3.22; pooled -4.57/-2.03. Held-out ranking: scratch fit +0.47/+0.56/+0.48 vs fit-free +0.50; pretrained fit +0.29/+0.50/+0.35 vs fit-free +0.61; pooled +0.40/+0.46/+0.41 vs +0.55. Caption explicitly disclaims coefficient ratios as normalization-sensitive.

Leave-one-architecture-out: scratch weights transfer (rho +0.51--0.65); pretrained fitted weights do NOT transfer between the two backbone architectures (held-out +0.25/+0.46 vs fit-free recall rule's +0.44/+0.67 on the same contexts); no nonlinear combiner (interaction, lexicographic, GBM, etc.) beats the 2-coefficient fit held out.

Decision utility: policy median top-1 regret 1.2/2.1/2.8 PCK (source/bench/both held out) vs matched-direction 3.9/4.7/3.9, summed 3.1/3.1/2.7, DINO 14.7/8.0/14.2, random 13.9; pairwise accuracy (gap>10) policy 0.77/0.78/0.78 vs retraining same-architecture 0.84 and different-architecture 0.78; per-regime split: pretrained matched-direction regret 0.7--2.1 vs sum's ~3.0, scratch sum 3.9--4.1 vs matched direction 5.2--7.9.

supp.summary: The ACCV 2026 supplement (/home/spencer/Projects/OnlineSyntheticCorrespondence/ACCV_2026/supp_main.tex, titled "Supplementary Material: Off-Target Mass or Missing Support?") provides six things. (1) Sec. supp:law gives the full per-variant evidence for the regime-direction principle: tab_supp_asym repeats main-paper Table 1 (identical numbers to tables/tab_law.tex) and adds FID/SW2/MMD symmetric baselines, claiming the rule's margin is largest where the directions disagree most (pretrained GLU-Net: rule +0.67/+0.76 vs sym +0.26/+0.33); tab_supp_eps replicates the rule with an epsilon-radius coverage estimator at 1/4/16 px, claiming the rule-over-symmetric margin at 4-16 px exceeds the mean-NN margin while 1 px "saturates"; tab_supp_dino is the appearance-space negative control (all directed correlations -0.15 to -0.35, flip statistic +0.018, p=0.43). (2) Sec. supp:robust (tab_supp_controls, baseline rule rho = +0.507) reports a shuffle null of -0.000 (200 perms, claimed p<0.005), generator-family drops (+0.425 to +0.544), benchmark drops ([+0.495, +0.532]), and size controls (n samples +0.043, n vectors +0.267). (3) Sec. supp:predict gives per-variant reproducibility oracles (pretrained GLU-Net fractions of oracle O2 reach +1.37/+1.31, claimed "fractions >1.3" though the O3 fractions are +1.26/+1.14); gap-stratified pairwise accuracy (rule 0.624/0.652/0.629 overall vs retraining agreement 0.736/0.696 — rule below retraining in every bin, near chance at 0.551-0.569 for sub-1-PCK gaps); a feature-set ablation (mean-NN best for scratch ranking, coverage edges pretrained, appearance max +0.13 though the text says "rho <= 0.16"; the claim that the combined set "gives the best absolute error" is contradicted by epsilon-4px pretrained MAE 7.9 < combined 8.0); a no-table claim that directional anchor interpolation loses to symmetric IDW (16.9 vs 18.9-24.1 held-out-benchmark MAE; 8.6 vs 8.7-10.1 held-out-source); an exclusion note for the pretrained arm of the intervention grid (3 sources whose d_TB and d_BT "orderings coincide", agreeing with transfer on "2 of 3 benchmarks") that CONTRADICTS the main paper's account of the same arm (main.tex ~line 849 reports distinct unstable estimates d_TB +0.64, d_BT +0.31, sym +0.43 "nominally favor[ing] the unmatched direction" — impossible if the orderings coincide); and the full BFV recovery table (KITTI-2015: dolly 2.18, vert. frac 0.001, "camera-centric"; FlyingThings: dolly 0.32, vert. frac 0.920, "object-centric") together with an explicit admission that BFV is blind to the camera/object factorization it is being used to recover. (4) Sec. supp:sampling justifies mean-NN/coverage estimators (rho >= 0.96 at 5e4 vectors, 1.000 at reference; kNN-KL plateaus at 0.5/0.2 and never stabilizes) over "all 110 train->benchmark pairs" — a count that implies 10 benchmarks (11 sources x 10), i.e. includes Middlebury, while the paper's stance is 9 benchmarks; it also concedes the intervention-grid d_TB ranking is "estimator-noise-limited even after 5-seed averaging", which directly qualifies the main paper's pre-registered out-of-sample test. (6) Four figures decompose the absolute predictor into ranking (median per-benchmark slope 0.43-0.51) and level (per-trainset slope 0.93-0.96) and show the closed-loop intervention. Overall the supplement is broadly consistent with the main story but contains one genuine cross-document contradiction (the pretrained grid arm), several text-vs-own-table overstatements (oracle fractions, combined-MAE, "no flip exists" vs RAFT's DINO flip CI [+0.02,+0.16], missing supervision-density row), and several honest admissions that soften the main story (rule below retraining agreement in all gap bins, partial epsilon-replication exactly where the law is strongest, BFV camera/object blind spot, noise-limited d_TB on the intervention family).

vaultProject.summary: The Obsidian vault records a narrative that pivoted four times in roughly ten days. (1) Pre-June baseline: the rejected ECCV submission led with directed coverage + SDF-Fractal3D as the main novelty. (2) The 2026-05-28/06-05 reframe (Overview.md, Paper 2 - Outline, codex_analysis 06-07): headline = "motion-domain cross-distance predicts within-context transfer; appearance (DINO) does not," with perf = L + g, three CV regimes (LOTO/LOBO/JOINT), motion_sym (FID+SW2+MMD) recommended as the headline family, the closed interventional loop (KITTI predicted +0.93 vs actual +0.87, FlyingThings negative control) and robustness battery as the strength. The Advisor Audit (06-04) blessed exactly this version ("Project 2 scientific core ~80-90% complete, manuscript ~35-45%"), demanded the causal/SDF/directed-coverage claims be retired, and ordered a scope freeze for the June-22 dissertation draft. (3) The 06-08/09 intervention-grid phase (Session note, ACCV Camera-Ready Assessment 06-09): the 13-cell from-scratch grid opened dynamic range and tempted a "structure ≫ diversity" spine swap, but the assessment ruled the prediction-spine version "the only one writable today" and flagged single-seed Tier-2 claims, the dead "appearance nearly free (−0.37)" framing (corrected to −2.74), and stale-number inconsistencies. (4) The 06-09/10 Regime-Direction Law (Regime-Direction Law note, Briefing v2, Outline v2, Results Tables, Kitchen Sink): the latest written framing — WHICH direction of directed motion coverage predicts transfer flips with training regime (scratch = precision-bound by off-target mass d(T→B); pretrained = recall-bound by missing support d(B→T)), flip statistic +0.899, exact permutation p=0.0286 (RAFT excluded) / 0.0079 (RAFT as scratch), no flip in DINO space; a fit-free if-statement rule reaches ρ≈0.50-0.51 on all three splits (~the reproducibility ceiling), and a pre-registered out-of-sample test on the 13-cell Kubric grid PASSED (FF arm matched direction +0.656 vs sym −0.011 vs mismatched −0.261). This explicitly inverts the 06-05 framing: symmetric metrics, formerly the recommended headline, become "the direction-blind hedge — decent everywhere, best nowhere," the fitted ridge is demoted to an ablation, and the original ECCV directed-coverage idea is rehabilitated ("washed out only because pooling cancels the two directions"). vaultExperiments.summary: The project's evidence base rests on four layers. (1) CORRELATIONAL HEADLINE: motion-space (optical-flow) source→benchmark distances predict transfer rankings of synthetic training sources far better than matched DINO appearance distances, across three CV regimes (LOTO held-source, LOBO held-benchmark, JOINT both held). The headline estimand is the paired motion-minus-appearance gap under generator-family cluster bootstrap (gap +0.364 to +0.754, P(gap>0) >= 0.993 in all regimes), defended by shuffle nulls, 6-way L-mechanism invariance, density controls, leave-one-generator-family-out (motion rho stays +0.219 to +0.518 under every drop), and dense/sparse stratification. (2) CEILING FRAMING: the modest motion rho ~= 0.45 is reframed as ~78% of an inter-variant reproducibility ceiling (0.454/0.584 pooled) and 77%/79%/57% of a held-architecture consensus (LOTO/LOBO/JOINT); the win-rate-vs-gap analysis shows motion ranks source pairs about as well as re-training the model does at every gap size. The consistency analysis decomposes everything into level + source_quality + motion_match + noise: a seed-free camera-vs-object crossover (camera-dominant source wins K2012 by +6.99 FF / +2.67 TT; object-dominant wins FlyingThings by -5.46 FF / -3.65 TT, replicating across both training regimes) proves a genuine source-by-benchmark interaction, and double-demeaning shows the notorious appearance "anti-correlation" (+0.249 wrong-signed) is a source-quality confound that collapses to -0.175 once source identity is removed. (3) REGIME-DIRECTION LAW (newest, paper-restructuring): which DIRECTION of directed motion coverage predicts transfer flips with training regime — from-scratch models are precision-bound (train->target distance, a->b: catspp F/F +0.600) while pretrained models are recall-bound (target->train, b->a: glunet T/T +0.719); a fit-free one-bit regime rule scores +0.498 mean within-context Spearman, ~= the inter-variant ceiling 0.528 (fraction 0.99), beats every fitted ridge/pooling structure, was adversarially verified (exact permutation p=0.0286, the design's floor), and PASSED its pre-registered out-of-sample test on the from-scratch kubric intervention grid (precision +0.621 > sym +0.096 > recall -0.125 with 5-seed-averaged distances); a DINO control shows no flip in appearance space. (4) INTERVENTIONAL STUDY (kubric/SDF renders): the practical loop "search synthetic-motion parameters theta with TPE against the predictor, materialize the winner, train, compare to prediction" is supposed to show the predictor can DESIGN data, not just analyze it. It is closed for KITTI (predicted margin +0.93 vs observed +0.87; trial76 97.78 vs anchor 96.91) and confirmed as an honest null on FlyingThings (predicted ~0; trained trial80 80.68 vs baseline 82.26 = -1.58); the kubric arm produced a 13-cell master table where trial19 (single frozen forward-dolly) beats movi_f on K2015 (96.12 vs 94.82 TT; 87.15 #1 from-scratch) and the TPE-designed synthetic_fractal is the strongest from-scratch source (94.43 K2015). FAILURES/INCONSISTENCIES are significant and well-documented: a Middlebury eval bug was CONFIRMED 2026-06-10 and Middlebury is now EXCLUDED from all canonical results — most Obsidian-note tables quoting Middlebury numbers predate this; the trial19 training set was discovered to be DEGENERATE (one frozen motion field x 5000 textures), which converted the "appearance is nearly free" -0.37 HQ->matte result into a frozen-set artifact (with real motion diversity the matte cost is -2.57 to -2.74 at TT and -3.7 to -10.8 from scratch); the predictor's known object-blindness made it wrongly predict the FT-recovered config would be a strong KITTI source; absolute-level calibration misses by ~4-19 PCK out of distribution and two leakage-clean calibration analyses returned NULL (ranking, not magnitude, is the deliverable); almost all intervention cells are single-seed with variant gaps at or below the +-0.4-1.9 seed-noise floor; and the from-scratch arm's fine K2015 ordering flips against motion distance and is attributed to seed noise plus a clean-supervision confound. Current state of the interventional arm: FF grid 10/10 complete, jitter (randomness-ladder) dataset and KITTI-fitted HQ/matte pairs still materializing, sdf Middlebury/FlyingThings TPE winners searched but never trained, and >=3-seed runs on the load-bearing crossover cells remain the decisive missing validation.

eccv.summary: The ECCV 2026 submission (paper 'Beyond Realism: Directed Coverage for Correspondence Transfer', sources in /home/spencer/Projects/ECCV_Reviews/eccv2026/) claimed that photorealism is not the sole driver of sim-to-real transfer for dense correspondence: SDF-Fractal3D, an asset-free non-photorealistic procedural pipeline, transfers strongly zero-shot across ~10 benchmarks; 'directed coverage' (asymmetric overlap separating missing target support E->T from off-target mass T->E in motion/appearance descriptor spaces) feeds a compact ridge estimator reaching 'up to 0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy' under three held-out protocols (best row F×2+A×2: 70.1/69.8/69.4%), and motion-only zoom/flip interventions move transfer as predicted (KITTI-2015 90.43 -> 94.94 with large-zoom, 84.72 with flip). Three reviewers, all negative: A (aL7M, Reject, conf 4) — unclear motivation, observation-driven narrative written as method-driven, missing SDF-Fractal3D sample counts, '0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy is not very useful', Table 4 changes small, architecture averaging obscures behavior; B (X9xv, Borderline Reject, conf 2, open to raising) — BFV outlier/long-tail normalization robustness, performance ceiling vs other datasets, ridge generalization to temporal/4D architectures, dataset-size-as-nuisance, absolute-vs-ranking, 2D-warp confound on the motion-primary claim; C (mqfN, Weak Reject, conf 5, expert) — causal claims exceed evidence (many confounds beyond realism; interventions limited to one synthetic family), directed coverage heuristic/under-justified, 0.70 only moderate, mixed regimes + averaging muddy interpretation, missing realism-only control, narrow baselines, incremental novelty. The current ACCV draft direction directly targets most of this: SDF-Fractal3D is demoted from headline to instrument (P-001/P-002/S-004); the headline becomes the regime-direction / two-cost law validated per-variant across 3 architectures × 9 variants × 11 pure synthetic sources × 9 benchmarks (891 evaluations, no averaging, no mixed regimes — S-006/S-019/S-020); '0.70 not useful' is answered by ceiling parity (rho≈0.5 ≈ inter-variant reproducibility ceiling, 73-76% of retraining consensus), selection regret (median 1.2-2.8 PCK vs 13.9 random), and gap-stratified accuracy (0.77-0.78 = cross-arch retraining at gaps >10 PCK) (P-007/P-013); causal overreach is met with a pre-registered out-of-sample grid test (off-target cost rho=+0.67, 8/9 flip p=0.029, appearance null p=0.43) plus an honest Limitations (P-012/S-015/S-016); absolute-vs-ranking gets its own section (P-009); the ridge-is-feature-engineering critique is inverted (fit-free policy beats every learned model — S-018); the HQ/matte texture-twin 2×2 supplies the missing realism-only control and recalibrates motion-primacy to specificity-not-magnitude (S-021/P-010, off-diagonal ties 91.1 vs 89.5); estimator unification (mean-NN + epsilon-coverage + KL contrast, HOF dropped) answers S-017/S-010/S-014. Still NOT addressed: BFV extreme-flow/outlier handling (S-007/S-008, no winsorization/clipping discussion found), SDF-Fractal3D training sample counts (S-003, not found), temporal/point-tracking architectures (S-013 — FlowFormer only pre-registered, results pending), modern transferability-estimator baselines (S-022 partial), and the pretrained half of the new law itself is observational-only — structurally the same gap Reviewer C punished. Notable internal red flag: the ECCV submission's Middlebury column came from a later-confirmed-buggy eval harness; ACCV excludes Middlebury entirely.

repoDocs.summary: Five working documents plus one script describe the Regime-Direction Law project at three successive moments, and they have drifted apart. glunet_modeling.md (Jun 9, 21:26) establishes the precursor problem: adding GLU-Net to the shared 3-architecture ridge diluted the pooled motion headline from 0.51/0.45/0.32 to 0.31/0.36/0.18 (LOTO/LOBO/JOINT) and hurt CATs++/RAFT per-variant numbers; its Section 9 resolution is a two-pool fit (CATs+++RAFT pooled reproduces 0.52/0.46/0.31; GLU-Net fit separately) with consensus fraction 0.63/0.71/0.39 of the 0.731 ceiling, and it explicitly retracts an earlier "0.619 to 0.731 ceiling" comparison as confounded. REGIME_DIRECTION_FINDING.md (Jun 9, 23:15) supersedes the two-pool framing with the law itself: scratch models are precision-bound (train-to-target distance predicts transfer), pretrained models recall-bound (target-to-train); a fit-free one-bit regime rule scores +0.498 mean within-context Spearman, essentially at the inter-variant ceiling (+0.528, fraction ~0.99), beating every fitted pooling structure; it documents an adversarial verification (flip +0.818, exact permutation p=0.0286), a passed pre-registered out-of-sample FF-arm test on the kubric intervention grid (precision +0.621 vs recall -0.125 vs sym +0.096), a DINO negative control (no flip, p=0.54), and rule-based consensus 0.79/0.80/0.81 of 0.731. RESULTS_TABLES.md (Jun 9, 23:43) consolidates these into tables T1-T9, opening with "Every number below is on disk now; nothing pending" -- a claim that is no longer true. HANDOFF_tt_grid_parity.md (Jun 10, 13:18) diagnoses why the OOS pretrained (TT) arm had only 3 sources vs FF's 10 (un-harvested old snapshots) and prescribes 6 harvests + 1 verify + 1 retrain plus removal of a hardcoded trial19 96.1158 line in blocks.py. run_clean_pipeline.sh regenerates the now-superseded shared-ridge v4 results and still fits a middlebury predictor; score_synthetic_fractal.py rescores the trial76 FF cell on four benchmarks including middlebury. Cross-checking disk state reveals the handoff WAS executed on Jun 10 (4 symlinks at 13:21, lowtex_matte and trial76 TT trained 13:28, trial19 TT retrained 18:09, hardcode removed), and two downstream regenerations occurred that neither finding doc reflects: (1) the verification REPORT.md was re-run Jun 10 12:47 with Middlebury excluded (891 rows, 9 benchmarks), shifting every per-variant rho (flip statistic now +0.899, not +0.818; catspp F/F precision +0.527 not +0.558/+0.600; glunet T/T recall +0.763 not +0.734/+0.719; RAFT d +0.098 not +0.22) -- so THREE versions of the law's headline table coexist; (2) intervention_oos.csv was regenerated Jun 10 21:11 without middlebury and with the TT arm at n=9, and the new TT-arm correlations show precision GREATER than recall on all three benchmarks (flyingthings 0.733 vs 0.083; kitti2012 0.800 vs 0.650; kitti2015 0.383 vs -0.100) -- the face-value OPPOSITE of the law's pretrained-recall prediction, recorded nowhere in any document. The FF-arm PASS survives Middlebury removal (its three remaining per-benchmark values match T7 exactly). trial19's TT retrain peaks at 96.37 K2015, rank 4/10 in the TT arm -- consistent with the handoff's "mid-pack" prediction but making the documented "rank 2/4" and the hardcoded 96.1158 stale.
